QF.id: AIFM Fund Monitoring, Reporting, and Exit_1

question.text: Ms. Priya Shah, Fund Manager at Saraswati Capital AIF (Category II), is preparing the annual LP report for FY ending 31-Mar. By which date must the report be dispatched to investors under Regulation 22 of the SEBI (AIF) Regulations?

answer.text: Within 60 days of financial year-end (i.e., by 30-May)
Within 90 days of financial year-end (i.e., by 29-Jun)
Within 180 days of financial year-end (i.e., by 27-Sep)
Within 30 days of financial year-end (i.e., by 30-Apr)

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Regulation 22 read with SEBI circulars requires AIFs other than Category III to furnish the annual report to investors within 180 days from the end of the financial year. Category III AIFs report quarterly within 60 days of quarter-end. Hence 180 days (27-Sep) is correct for Saraswati Capital, a Cat II fund. **The Trap:** 60 days is the Cat III quarterly deadline — a common mix-up. 90 days mimics a typical statutory audit timeline but is not the SEBI AIF rule. 30 days applies to the activity report filed with SEBI (post-quarter), not LP reporting. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-A (Cat I/II Distributor) tests the same 180-day rule from the investor-disclosure angle. XIX-B (Cat III Distributor) emphasises the 60-day quarterly window. XXI-B (PM) instead uses SEBI's 30-day monthly client reporting under the PM Regulations — do not conflate. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Build the annual report a full month before the 180-day deadline — auditor sign-off on portfolio-company financials routinely slips in Indian GPs, and an LPAC escalation for late delivery is the single most avoidable hit to your next-fund reference calls.
